scenes.headline: How GLiNER2.5 finds entities without a width limit
scenes.sub: Boundary scores instead of span enumeration, and joint decoding under schema rules.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bloop! GLiNER2.5 is a small encoder that turns text into structured records. Here's the one change behind the whole release.

scenes.text: It stopped enumerating spans and started scoring boundaries. A forty-word clause now costs exactly what a two-word name costs to locate.
scenes.say: The idea: stop enumerating spans, and score boundaries instead. A forty-word clause then costs exactly what a two-word name costs to find.

scenes.title: Every candidate span, as a cell

steps.label: Older GLiNER: widths up to max_width
steps.say: Every candidate span is a cell: a start and an end. Older versions scored only widths up to a maximum. Longer entities weren't scored at all.

steps.label: GLiNER2.5: any start, any end
steps.say: This version deletes that axis. An entity may start at the first token and end at the last.

scenes.title: From boundaries to a valid graph

steps.say: The encoder reads the text and the schema's queries together.
For each query it scores every boundary: how likely a span starts here, ends here, or sits inside.
It pairs the best few starts with the best few ends, however far apart, and a reranker scores each pair.
Entities and relations are decoded together, checked against the schema's rules as they're built. So no edge points at a missing node.

scenes.label: read in one pass: dropping span representations freed the memory
scenes.note: longer documents: overlapping chunks, offsets remapped to the original
scenes.say: Dropping explicit span representations also freed the memory to train at four thousand ninety-six words. Longer documents get overlapping chunks, mapped back to the source.

scenes.label: 16-benchmark macro-F1, the 0.3B checkpoint against GLiNER2: parity
scenes.note: drop XNLI: 0.3B is 1.57 behind, 0.2B is 1.27 ahead
scenes.say: On accuracy, the claim is parity. At the larger checkpoint, one dataset carries it: drop XNLI and it trails by one point five seven. The smaller one gains broadly.

scenes.text: The change was subtraction. Delete the width axis, and a small encoder returns validated structure, not just entities.

recap: No width ceiling; 4,096 words per pass
Entities and relations decoded under rules
scenes.say: To recap: scored boundaries, no width ceiling, and a graph that's valid by construction.
